chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Wassafi, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is pleased if Allah were to extend his lifespan and expand his sustenance, let him maintain goodly relations with his kin, for the kinship has a tongue on the Day of Resurrection, eloquent, saying: O Lord! Maintain relationship with the one who maintained it with me, and cut off the one who cut me off.'
So the man would be seen to be on the goodly way, when the kinship that he had cut off comes to him, so it would plunge with him into the lowest depth into the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of maintaining family ties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores silat al-rahim as a divine mechanism for sustaining worldly blessings, linking physical longevity and material provision to spiritual fidelity. The metaphor of the womb's 'eloquent tongue' (lisān dhallāq) personifies kinship as an active intercessor on the Day of Judgment, reinforcing the concept that severing ties invites immediate spiritual descent to the lowest depths of Hell (asfal al-ārfīn).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al Wassafy, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is joyful if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> were to Extend in his life-span, and Expand for him in his sustenance, so let him maintain goodly relations with the relatives, for the kinship, there would be an eloquent tongue for it on the Day of Judgement, saying, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Maintaining Relationship with the one who maintained it with me, and Cut off the one who cut me off’.
So the man would be seen to be on the goodly way, when the kinship comes to whim which he had cut if off, so it would plunge with him into the lowest depth into the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 29. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from al-Wassafi from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever loves Allah’s giving him a long life and increasing his means of sustenance, he should maintain good relations with relatives; kindred relation, will have a sharp tongue on the Day of Judgment and it will say, “O Lord, establish good relations with those who maintained me properly and cut off those who cut me off.
A man could be seen on the ways of good deeds but when the kindred relation that he had cut off would come he will be thrown into the depth of fire.’”
